title: Orbital
tagline: One burn. After that it is just gravity.
description: Twelve launches, each with exactly one decision: which way to point and how hard to push. After that the probe belongs to the planets, and the only way to reach the ring is to fall past something heavy at the right distance. The line you aim with is the real trajectory, computed the same way the flight is — so if the preview reaches, the probe reaches.
author: HexCave
controls: Hold to charge, release to launch
Arrow keys also aim; R retries
howToPlay: Move the mouse to aim. The dotted line is the actual trajectory, computed the same way the flight is — if the dots reach the ring, the probe will too.
Hold the mouse button, or space, to build power. Release to launch.
You get one burn. After that the probe belongs to the planets and you can only watch.
The dots bunch together where the probe is moving slowly, which is the clearest sign you are about to be captured by something.
Falling past a planet bends the path — most levels can only be reached by using that, not by aiming straight at the target.
Crashing or flying off into space costs you nothing but another attempt. Press R to reset the aim.
goal: Put the probe through the ring on each of the twelve launches. Every level has been proved reachable.
